newsitem.title: USA: Intel buys computer graphics supplier.
newsitem.headline: Intel buys computer graphics supplier.

text.p: Computer chip maker Intel Corp. said Monday it agreed to acquire Chips and Technologies Inc., a supplier of graphics for personal computers, for $397 million.
Intel said it will pay $17.50 a share for each Chips and Technologies share. The company, based in San Jose, Calif., has 22.7 million shares outstanding.
Chips and Technologies stock jumped $3.125 to $17.125 and Intel was down $1.19 at $88, both in early trading on Nasdaq.
With the acquisition, Intel intends to advance capabilities for graphics and visual computing in mobile personal computers, it said.
"Intel and Chips and Technologies already share an excellent working relationship based on our joint efforts in graphics accelerators," said Craig R. Barrett, Intel president.
"Intel's acquisition of Chips and Technologies will provide us with the ability to bring strong graphics solutions to the mobile market segment." he said.
Chips and Technologies will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Intel Corp. and part of Intel's Graphics Components Division, Intel said.
Jim Stafford, Chips and Technologies' president and chief executive officer, will join Intel as a vice president of the company's Desktop Products Group.
Current Chips and Technologies employees will become employees of Intel, and Intel said it does not anticipate any immediate changes to Chips and Technologies' product line.
